issue.title: artifact-link rename repair (_historical_rename_map) has no time budget on its per-ref git subprocess loop
issue.description:
Discovered while implementing plans/202608/artifact_link_backfill_chop_timeout.md,
which fixed the artifact_link_backfill housekeeping chop's recurring 300s timeout by
hoisting artifact-ref context resolution out of the reconcile row loop (fix verified:
preview_reconciled_aggregate dropped from ~223s to ~12-15s on gh_sase-org__sase,
byte-identical output before/after).

That plan's chop guardrail adds a whole-chop `_CHOP_WORK_BUDGET_SECONDS` deadline check
in src/sase/scripts/sase_chop_artifact_link_backfill.py, checked before starting each
project and between jobs 2/3/4. But job 3 (reconcile) and job 4 (rename repair) are
bundled into one call, `reconcile_and_repair_artifact_links()`, so the deadline can only
be checked before that combined call starts, not during job 4's internal work.

Job 4's `repair_historical_artifact_renames` shells out to `git` once per candidate
dangling ref inside `_historical_rename_map`, with no per-call or per-project time
budget -- unlike the sweep job, which already has `_SWEEP_WORK_BUDGET_SECONDS`. For
gh_sase-org__sase this was 208 `git` subprocess calls in one profiled run, dominating
cumulative time (`ncalls` for `_historical_rename_map`/`run_sdd_git` matched the 208
dangling refs needing a rename lookup).

Measured wall-clock cost for the combined reconcile+repair call was highly variable
across two runs minutes apart on the same host/repo: 18.3s in a standalone cProfile
run vs. 98.18s in an actual `sase axe chop run artifact_link_backfill` invocation (its
progress log recorded `gh_sase-org__sase: done in 100.65s (sweep=0.72s, drain=1.74s,
reconcile_repair=98.18s)`). The now-fixed reconcile pass itself is bounded (~12-15s);
essentially all of the variance and remaining cost is job 4's unbounded git-subprocess
loop.

task_type_fields.impact:
This chop's own 300s timeout is not currently reintroduced -- the outer chop finished
in ~100-105s total in every run observed so far, well under both the new 240s chop
budget and the axe 300s hard timeout. But job 4's cost is unbounded and
git-subprocess-count-dependent, so it is a latent tail-latency risk for this chop (and
for `sase artifact doctor`, which calls the same `reconcile_and_repair_artifact_links`
path) if the number of dangling refs grows or disk/git performance regresses on a given
run. A single project's rename-repair step could then consume most or all of the
remaining chop budget in one shot, since the chop-level deadline check cannot interrupt
work already in flight.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_renames.py:69 (repair_historical_artifact_renames) and :323 (_historical_rename_map, the per-ref git subprocess loop via run_sdd_git in src/sase/sdd/_git.py:32)
task_type_fields.repro:
Run against a real store with a project that has dangling artifact-link refs (e.g.
gh_sase-org__sase on this host):

```python
import cProfile, pstats, time
from pathlib import Path
from sase.sdd.artifact_link_store import resolve_artifact_link_store
from sase.sdd.artifact_link_backfill import reconcile_and_repair_artifact_links

store = resolve_artifact_link_store(cwd=Path("/home/bryan/projects/github/sase-org/sase/"))
pr = cProfile.Profile(); pr.enable()
t0 = time.monotonic()
reconcile_and_repair_artifact_links(store)
print(time.monotonic() - t0)
pr.disable()
pstats.Stats(pr).sort_stats("cumulative").print_stats(10)
```

`_historical_rename_map` (src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_renames.py:323) and
`run_sdd_git` (src/sase/sdd/_git.py:32) dominate cumulative time, with one `git`
subprocess call per candidate dangling ref and no budget on the loop. Also reproducible
end-to-end via `sase axe chop run artifact_link_backfill -L housekeeping -f -V`, whose
per-project progress log line reports the `reconcile_repair` elapsed seconds for each
project.

payload.description: the likely upstream cause: an artifact_link_backfill chop whose job 4 has no time budget cannot finish the reconciliation job that keeps this aggregate converged

evidence.note: Independent reproduction 2026-08-28: ~/.sase/axe/recent_errors.json still holds 13 ('housekeeping','artifact_link_backfill') entries in the 100-error ring. 12 of 13 are 'timed out after 300s' (2026-08-26T06:42 through 2026-08-27T13:04), matching this bead's unbounded job-4 git loop. The 13th is a later 2026-08-28T07:29:13 'exit code 1' JSONDecodeError in read_artifact_link_index while rebuild_aggregate parsed a sidecar index (Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 16 column 1). Subsequent hourly ticks today succeeded (08:48, 09:48, 10:06, 10:30 all structured result ok; sase reconcile_repair still 126-198s). Timeout risk remains; the JSONDecodeError is a separate fail-closed gap on one corrupt sidecar.

payload.description: Both are defects in sase.sdd callers of run_sdd_git (src/sase/sdd/_git.py:32); sase-u9 hits its unbounded per-ref subprocess loop, sase-va hits its text=False default leaving stderr as bytes

evidence.note: Independent reproduction 2026-09-03 (bbugyi's athena host, sase_14 workspace agent): the latent tail-latency risk is now a persistent hard failure — 5 consecutive housekeeping ticks died with 'timed out after 300s' (12:44, 14:26, 15:31, 16:36, 16:44; digest_20260903_173941.txt). Live observation of the 17:39 run (chop PID 76109): ps sampling showed a FRESH 'git log --all --format= --name-status --find-renames -M --diff-filter=R' child process every 1-2s for 3.5+ minutes, cwd=/Users/bbugyi/projects/github/sase-org/sase/sase/repos/plans (6222 commits across refs; one scan timed at ~2.2s wall). ROOT CAUSE SHARPENED beyond 'no time budget': repair_historical_artifact_renames at src/sase/sdd/_artifact_link_renames.py:89-92 calls by_kind.setdefault(kind, _historical_rename_map(root, kind=kind)) — Python evaluates setdefault's default EAGERLY, so the full-history rename scan runs once per dangling ref instead of once per kind. The intended memoization exists but is dead code; fixing it bounds job 4 to <=2 scans (~5s) per project. Failure onset pattern also explained: while the retroactive sweep still had remaining docs, _run_project returned before job 4 ('deferred outbox/reconcile after sweep budget'); once the sweep converged (13 remaining at 13:22, then 0), job 4 finally ran for gh_sase-org__sase every tick and each tick died in it. A fix plan (memoization guard + deadline threading into reconcile_and_repair_artifact_links) is being proposed this turn.

payload.description: Both surfaced as artifact_link_backfill error digests on athena; this fd crash produced the 'exit code 1' digests that masked sase-u9's 300s timeouts for most of 2026-09-03
The corroborated task bead this plan fixes and closes.
